commitResults.messageTitle: Add guardian contact CRUD for students
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors need to manage one optional guardian contact per student
without changing the student's other details.

Add separate guardian commands, display contacts in student cards,
and reuse existing JSON persistence. Document the workflow and test
field preservation, validation, filtering and automatic saving.

Validation: 329 tests, Checkstyle and JavaFX card checks pass.

commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the dark AB3 theme with a light one. The student list shows a
count and an empty state that tells an empty book apart from a search
with no matches. Cards show every current field, with placeholders for
missing details, and long text wraps. A command panel at the bottom
marks results as success or error.

Card numbers still follow the filtered list, so they match command
indices. Logic exposes the address book so the list can count all
students.
Create lesson object

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master with lesson model into ui-student-list
commitResults.messageBody:
Show each student's lessons as a numbered list, so the numbers match
LESSON_INDEX, and update the guides to the new card text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Format command help and add keyboard shortcuts
commitResults.messageBody:
Show usage errors as a heading, a description, and labelled Format
and Example lines in a monospace font, so a mistyped command can be
fixed from the message alone.

Keyboard users can now recall earlier commands with Up and Down, clear
the box with Esc, scroll the list with Page Up and Page Down while
typing, and close help with Esc. Key hints show while the box is empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy planning guides and add tentative dates
commitResults.messageBody:
Reword process notes as team guidance, add the tentative v1.5 date
and PE window from the course site, and link the team documents in
view mode.

commitResults.messageTitle: Colour-code cards and address review findings
commitResults.messageBody:
Colour the level chip by school stage and show each lesson's mode as
a coloured chip. Levels in unrecognised forms stay neutral.

Also from review: darker muted text for contrast, click-to-copy for
command formats and examples, wrapping for long emails and guardian
names, a drawn success mark, key hints hidden in narrow windows,
tests that run every real usage message, and an updated UI diagram.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show lessons as an aligned table on student cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Line up each lesson's number, subject, time and rate in columns, with
the mode tag and location on a second line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Link team documents as read-only published pages
Show students as a table with a lesson breakdown
commitResults.messageBody:
Match the mockup's student table: one row per student with Student,
Lessons and Guardian columns, where each lesson's number, subject,
day and time, and rate line up. Bundle the Geist fonts (SIL OFL) and
use them throughout.

The Guardian column folds into the Student column in narrow windows,
and the minimum window width is now 760px so a lesson line always
fits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show one line per student with details on demand
commitResults.messageBody:
Each row now shows only the name, level, next lesson and guardian.
A student's full details (every lesson, contact details, guardian and
tags) open when a search leaves one student, with Alt+Up/Alt+Down from
the command box, or with a click; Esc in an empty box closes them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the mockup: sidebar, table and smooth details
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a sidebar with Students, the levels (each runs find level/X) and
All commands, a page header with an Add student button, and table
columns for subjects and rate. Details open and close with a short
grow and shrink animation; clicking an open row closes it, and the
cursor stays in the command box. Short successes show the recent
commands beside them; results fade in and errors give a small shake.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master: open on the week calendar from #66
commitResults.messageBody:
Bring in Jian Yi's weekly schedule grid and make it the main screen.
The app opens on "This week"; list and find show the student table,
and the new week command shows the calendar again, listing every
student so each lesson's "#3.1" label matches the command indices.

The calendar follows the mockup: dated day headings with today
circled and shaded, a current-time line, hour rows from 9am to 8pm
that stretch to fit, lesson blocks tinted by school stage, a colour
key, and headings that stay in view while scrolling. A day with
overlapping lessons widens instead of squeezing them.

Review fixes on the grid: times use the app's 9.00am format, the
layout files declare JavaFX 17, Lesson is no longer Comparable, the
calendar redraws when the date changes, detail keys do nothing while
the calendar shows, and the tooltip test no longer relies on hover.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep calendar blocks one column wide and fit a one-hour block
commitResults.messageBody: Lessons that overlap nothing keep the normal width on a day widened by overlaps, and a one-hour block now shows its name, time and details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make every feature easy to reach from the keyboard
commitResults.messageBody:
Add `view INDEX`, which opens a student's details on the table, so
a calendar lesson's rate, mode and location (#3.1 means `view 3`)
no longer need the mouse. On the calendar, Alt+Up/Down scrolls, so
laptops without Page Up/Down can move through the day; the hint
changes with the screen. Tab puts the shown Example in the command
box after a format error. Long results grow to 40% of the window
instead of scrolling, and the calendar opens at the current time.

The help window links to the StudentBook guide, shows the data file,
copies the link with Enter and returns focus to the command box.
The command panel is outlined while focused, Alt released after a
shortcut no longer focuses the menu bar, and the time line gets its
dot and a softer red.

commitResults.messageTitle: Put the command bar on top and calm the rest of the window
commitResults.messageBody:
The command box and its result now sit at the top of the window,
and everything around them is a shade darker, so the place to type
stands out in a CLI-first app. Lesson blocks lose their borders and
use soft level colours with a hairline gap; grid lines, labels and
cards are quieter, and today is gently lit. The current-time line is
a brighter red with a smaller dot.

Fix today's column hiding its hour lines, and replace the remaining
AddressBook wording ("persons", "Address book has been cleared!").

commitResults.messageTitle: Cut long recent commands short in their chips
commitResults.messageBody: A long command such as an add no longer stretches its chip across the result row; the full command shows on hover and is one Up away.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the window's focus owner in the Tab tests
commitResults.messageBody: isFocused() also needs the OS to focus the test window, so the tests failed whenever another app was in front.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move the sidebar into a row of tabs under the command bar
commitResults.messageBody:
The sidebar took width from the calendar and the table, and the team
asked for horizontal tabs and something above the command bar for the
eye to land on. The StudentBook name now sits above the command box,
and a row under it holds the This week and Students tabs, one filter
per level in use and All commands. Each tab still shows the command it
runs.

Level filters that do not fully fit are hidden, so a long level such
as "Secondary 1 Express" is never shown cut short as "Secondary".
Windows shorter than 560px hide the name and the data file footer, so
the 1280x720 at 150% minimum still shows three students.
Rename AddressBook references to StudentBook

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a working example command in the empty states
commitResults.messageBody:
The empty week and student screens showed the full parameter format in
grey, which was hard to read. They now say what to do in a short line
and show an example command, in the command font, that works if typed
as shown. A test runs both examples so they stay valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep student details on the same student when the list changes
commitResults.messageBody:
The table keeps the selected row number when the list changes, so
deleting the open student opened the next student's details. The
details now follow the student: an edit keeps them open, and a delete
closes them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the level filter test within a narrow screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The test widened the window to 1400px, wider than the macOS CI screen,
so the window stayed narrower and a filter stayed hidden. It now uses a
shorter last level and widens to 1000px.

commitResults.messageTitle: Measure how far the level filter test widens the window
commitResults.messageBody:
Text is wider on Linux than on macOS, so a fixed 1000px window was not
enough on the Ubuntu CI runner. The test now widens the window by what
the hidden filter needs on the system it runs on.

commitResults.messageTitle: Declare the fixed tabs and empty state in FXML
commitResults.messageBody:
The This week, Students and All commands tabs and the student list's
empty state never change shape, so they are now laid out in FXML like
the week screen's empty state. Java still builds the level filters,
which follow the levels in use. Also share the list's scroll lookup,
page fraction and column sizing, and remove an unused helper.
